input.quote: 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual but set at only one month of Fees "actually paid", far below the walk-away floor of six months' fees and below the preferred greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000. Worse, "without exception" overrides the otherwise well-drafted Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap. The redline raises the basis to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and restores the Excluded Claims carve-out; 21.3 already contains the required carve-outs and confirms Customer's payment obligations are not damages, so no further edit is needed.

proposal.summary: Raise mutual cap to greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and subject it to the Excluded Claims carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We raised the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, as a one-month cap is not a meaningful remedy. We also removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 — including indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches — sit outside the cap; if needed, we can accept a straight twelve months' Fees cap with those carve-outs preserved.

ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
